The premise is false. Hormozi did not tell a roofing company owner to stop door-knocking and move his budget into Google Ads. In his consulting session with the young roofing owner, he praised the owner's ability to door-knock as a core asset and told him to go all in on door-to-door sales as his primary growth engine, building a dedicated team rather than getting distracted by new channels. He did recommend Google Ads and digital marketing as a separate play for established service businesses, but for a startup relying on door-to-door sales, his advice was to double down on what already works.

If you are a service business owner weighing whether to scale door-knocking versus buying Google Ads, use the following decision criteria:

- **Channel Competence:** If you already know how to acquire customers profitably through direct outreach or door-knocking, maximize that channel first. Do not add paid digital channels until your primary outbound engine is fully scaled or constrained by team size.
- **Supply and Demand Constraints:** Determine whether your system is supply-constrained (you cannot deliver services fast enough) or demand-constrained (you lack leads). If demand is the constraint and you lack an outbound sales mechanism, digital ads are appropriate. 
- **Capital and Risk Tolerance:** Bootstrapped startups with more time and sweat equity than cash should prioritize high-volume outbound sales to preserve capital, whereas businesses with spare cash and proven unit economics should scale ad spend.
